text:
emily: Quick thread — seeing judge "flip" after mix in of quantized judge (gptq-3b-q4) for CI evals. Safety anchors are down ~6% vs FP16 judge. Can we triage?
omar: Ugh. Which anchor set? the safety_sentences_v2 or the new demographic_anchors?
emily: safety_sentences_v2 mainly, but I've spotted some demographic_anchors flips too.
trent: Can you paste the run id?
emily: run 2026-03-19-judgecal-342
lina: eval-bot just posted a summary: 

```
run: 2026-03-19-judgecal-342
judge: gptq-3b-q4
baseline_judge: fp16-3b
safety_anchor_accuracy: 86.2% -> 80.3% (-5.9)
demo_bias_gap: 3.4% -> 5.1% (+1.7)
notes: short-form prompts more affected
```

kevin: Can confirm quantization could change calibration. Two quick checks: 1) softmax temperature shift in judge scoring, 2) sampling nondeterminism around ties.
miguel: Also check tokenization differences if we're running different tokenizer builds for q models.
omar: Do we have the judge scoring distribution? histogram would help.
emily: attaching histogram in dashboard but quick paste: fp16 judge logits cluster mean 1.1 sigma, gptq mean 0.94 sigma — shifts tighten.
trent: Could be solved by simple score rescaling + a tie threshold. Proposal: when judge score delta < 0.03, mark tie and run adjudicator (ensemble) per config.
lina: +1. But we need CI gating: don't let a judge change propagate if safety anchors drop >2% w/o human review.
kevin: Agree. Suggest adding a CI check to our harness: 

```
if anchor_delta_safety <= 0.02: pass
else: fail_and_block_deploy('judge-calibration-regression')
```

miguel: For immediate mitigation, we can keep fp16 as primary judge and use gptq as secondary with weighted voting (0.7/0.3) until we calibrate.
emily: That seems sane. Steps:
- rollback primary judge to fp16 in CI (temporary)
- run controlled calibration job: pairwise logits, fit affine transform to match fp16 score distribution
- run fairness buckets across demographic_anchors
- add CI gating rule Lina suggested

trent: For the affine fit, use least-squares on validation anchors. Quick pseudo:

```
# fit a*score + b -> target_score
params = np.linalg.lstsq(X, y)
apply: adjusted = a*raw + b
```

omar: One more: log tie cases to new dashboard panel with examples + prompt context. We need sampling policy: 50 failing anchors + 200 random evals.
emily: I'll open a PR for the CI gating + dashboard tile. @miguel can you run the calibration job and post results here?
miguel: on it. kicking off: `./tools/eval_runner --suite judge-calibration --model gptq-3b-q4 --out /tmp/judgecal-342-calib`

eval-bot: New run completed: `/tmp/judgecal-342-calib` summary: 
- fitted affine: a=1.12 b=0.04
- post-adjust safety anchors: 86.0% (baseline 86.2%)
- bias gap: 3.6% (baseline 3.4%)
- CI diff now within 0.02

lina: Nice. That looks promising. Once Miguel uploads the fit artifact, add to model-serving config as `judge_score_adjustment` and flag in release notes.
kevin: We should also add a test in unit-level eval runner that asserts `tie_count` doesn't spike >1% after judge swap.
emily: Good call. I'll add both CI gate and unit test.
miguel: artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/judgecal/2019876543/affine.json
emily: Thanks all. We'll keep fp16 as default until next week rollout. Follow-ups: PRs by EOD, dashboard tile by Lina, CI rule by Emily, calibration artifact in model repo by Miguel.
trent: Can we add a short note to onboarding docs about judge quantization caveats? new note in /docs/evals/judge-ops.md
emily: yeah I'll draft it.
kevin: 👍
emily: closing loop, will update thread when PRs merge. :sparkles:
